records.question: How do I apply for it?
history: Can I work off campus during my first year if my program requires an internship?
records.search_query: How do I apply for it? | Can I work off campus during my first year if my program requires an internship?
records.answer:
Here is how to apply for CPT, based on the ISSS website. This also answers your earlier first-year question.

**First-year eligibility:** You generally must have been enrolled full-time in a degree-granting program and physically present in the U.S. for at least one full academic year (3 quarters or 2 semesters) before you're eligible. The exception is for graduate students whose programs require immediate participation in CPT.

**Steps:**
1. **Have an offer.** You need an internship or training offer directly related to your field of study.
2. **Confirm it's required.** The practical training must be required for all students in your program to graduate.
   - If you're in the co-op program, meet with your Steinbright Career Development Center Co-op Advisor first.
   - If you're not in co-op, meet with your academic advisor to confirm the training is required by your curriculum.
   - PhD students need secondary approval from the Office of Graduate Studies and a written statement from their PhD advisor explaining why the off-campus training is required for the dissertation.
3. **Submit your CPT application to ISSS** for final review. The forms are on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx).

**Other conditions:**
- If a course is tied to the requirement, you must be registered in it during the term your CPT is authorized.
- CPT is generally limited to 20 hours per week, with exceptions such as full-time co-op, breaks, or full-time required training.
- Don't start working until you're authorized.

**Date to note:** A DHS Final Rule is scheduled to take effect September 15, 2026. Students will receive a fixed Admit Until Date, and CPT can't continue past it unless you timely file an Extension of Stay. See the [ISSS announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/July/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Publishes-Final-Rule-Eliminating-Duration-of-Status).

Please confirm your own eligibility with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: When should I apply for it?
history: What is the STEM OPT extension?
records.search_query: When should I apply for it? | What is the STEM OPT extension?
records.answer:
**Timing for the STEM OPT extension:**

- **Earliest:** You can file up to 90 days before your Post-Completion OPT end date.
- **Latest:** USCIS must receive your application *before* your current OPT EAD card expires. If it doesn't, you won't be eligible for the extension.
- **Send documents to ISSS:** No later than 30 days before your OPT EAD end date, to allow time for processing and mailing.
- **60-day window:** USCIS must receive your application within 60 days of the date ISSS prints your STEM OPT Request I-20. Otherwise you'll need to redo your application.

**If your EAD expires while the application is pending:** If you applied on time, you may keep working up to 180 days past the expiration date with your valid I-797 receipt notice. Your STEM OPT EAD start date will be the day after your current EAD expires.

In practice, that means starting your I-983 and I-20 request well within the 90-day window, with your documents to ISSS at least 30 days before your EAD ends. Please confirm your specific dates with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: What about during summer break?
history: How many hours can I work on campus?
records.search_query: What about during summer break? | How many hours can I work on campus?
records.answer:
During an **approved vacation term**, immigration regulations allow F-1 and J-1 students to work **more than 20 hours per week** on campus. However, you must check with the Office of Human Resources for their own (non-immigration) policies on working during that time.

Some details to keep in mind:
- Per ISSS, a "vacation term" is the one term each year that F-1/J-1 students may take off. Quarter-system students can take it after three consecutive quarters, and semester-system students after two consecutive semesters. The excerpts don't say whether a regular summer break automatically counts as your approved vacation term, so please confirm with an ISSS advisor which term applies to you.
- You still need to be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, have not graduated, and have an unexpired I-20/DS-2019.
- J-1 students must get prior ISSS authorization for any on-campus job.
- If you are on co-op during the term, your co-op counts as your "class," so on-campus work is limited to 20 hours per week.

records.question: And for J-1 students?
history: How long is the grace period after F-1 students finish their program?
records.search_query: And for J-1 students? | How long is the grace period after F-1 students finish their program?
records.answer:
J-1 students (and their J-2 dependents) have a **30-day grace period** after their program ends.

**During the grace period you may:**
- Pack and prepare to leave the U.S.
- Travel within the United States

**You may not** work or study during this time.

**Other key points:**
- If you're not extending your status, you're expected to depart during the grace period. If you leave before it ends, you can't re-enter in J-1 status after your DS-2019 expiration date.
- The ISSS announcement says J visa holders also get the 30-day grace period after completing their programs, plus any time on Academic Training.

**Update on the rule change:** My earlier answer treated the duration-of-status change as only a proposal. That's outdated. On July 17, 2026, DHS published a final rule eliminating "duration of status" for F and J nonimmigrants. It was scheduled to take effect September 15, 2026, but is subject to congressional review, and DHS will publish the actual effective date or terminate the rule if that changes. The excerpts I have don't confirm the final effective date.

Under the final rule, J-1 students entering on or after the effective date would get a date-specific I-94 for a fixed period (up to four years). The excerpts don't say whether the J-1 30-day grace period changes. The earlier proposal only mentioned shortening the F-1 period, from 60 to 30 days. Since that proposal and the final rule may differ, and my F-1 answer relied on it, please confirm the current F-1 and J-1 grace periods with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How much money do I need to show for her?
history: Can I bring my wife to the U.S. while I study at Drexel?
records.search_query: How much money do I need to show for her? | Can I bring my wife to the U.S. while I study at Drexel?
records.answer:
For your wife, you need to show **$4,000** in additional funding. This is on top of the funds that cover your own tuition, fees, and living expenses, and it applies no matter how long she will stay in the U.S. (If you have children, it's $2,000 for each child.)

Your bank statement should be an updated official statement. For the general financial document standards ISSS lists (for example, typed and in English, on official bank letterhead or showing the bank name and address, no more than 4 months old, naming the account holder, and showing the currency, account type, and total available balance), see the New International Students page.

You submit this with the Add a Dependent form on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx), along with her passport copy and your proof of marriage.

Sources:

records.question: Can I travel abroad while it's pending?
history: How long does it take USCIS to approve it?
records.search_query: Can I travel abroad while it's pending? | How long does it take USCIS to approve it? | What is OPT?
records.answer:
It depends on which type of OPT you applied for and where you are in your program.

**Pre-Completion OPT:** You may travel and re-enter under the general F-1 travel requirements.

**Post-Completion OPT, before you finish your degree:** If you're returning to resume your studies, the general F-1 travel requirements apply.

**Post-Completion OPT, after finishing your degree (during the 60-day grace period):** ISSS says this may be "slightly risky." The F-1 regulations don't directly address it, but most students with a pending application have re-entered successfully with a copy of the USCIS receipt notice. If you travel, carry:
- Valid passport
- Valid F-1 visa sticker (Canada and Bermuda citizens are exempt)
- I-20 with OPT recommendation and a travel signature on page 2 that is **no older than 6 months**
- OPT receipt notice (mailed 2-3 weeks after USCIS receives your application)

**STEM OPT extension pending:** You should be able to re-enter if your current OPT has **not expired** when you return. If it has expired, travel may be risky. You'd also need to carry your expired OPT EAD, a letter from your STEM employer (job title, description, dates, salary), and the STEM OPT receipt notice. ISSS cannot guarantee entry, since Customs and Border Protection makes that decision.

**Note:** A January 2026 announcement says USCIS placed a hold on pending applications from nationals of certain travel ban countries. If that may apply to you, contact ISSS before applying or traveling.

Please confirm your travel plans with an ISSS advisor first.

records.question: What do I need to do before I come back?
history: I want to take a term off and go home next quarter.
records.search_query: What do I need to do before I come back? | I want to take a term off and go home next quarter.
records.answer:
Which steps apply depends on which option you use, so please confirm the details with an ISSS advisor. Here is what the ISSS website says.

**If you take an approved international break term (you keep your status):**
- You're expected to enroll full-time once the break ends.
- Before you leave, make sure you have a recent travel signature on your I-20 (F-1) or DS-2019 (J-1). Request one through the [Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs). The [Visa Renewal page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/visa-renewal) says you need a new signature if yours will be more than six months old when you return.
- Carry the documents needed for re-entry: a passport valid at least 6 months beyond your return date, a valid F-1/J-1 visa, and proof of enrollment such as a class schedule printout. The 2024 re-entry advisory lists these, and it is older news.
- If you need a new visa, the Visa Renewal page suggests a Drexel enrollment certification letter and up-to-date financial documents (funding documents more than 12 months old at the time of your visa application should be refreshed).
- Plan to return before the term starts, and allow time for travel delays. Check the [Academic Calendar](https://drexel.edu/provost/policies-calendars/academic-calendars).

**If your SEVIS record is terminated (extended leave or no LTFT eligibility):** The excerpts don't explain the steps for returning. Contact ISSS as soon as possible to discuss your plans and whether you intend to return.

records.question: Who is eligible for it?
history: What is Academic Training for J-1 students?
records.search_query: Who is eligible for it? | What is Academic Training for J-1 students?
records.answer:
To be eligible for Academic Training with Drexel, you must meet all of these requirements:

- **DS-2019 issued by Drexel**, not an outside agency (such as Fulbright).
- **Primary purpose is study:** you must be in the U.S. primarily to study, not to do academic training.
- **Good academic standing.**
- **Related to your major:** the AT must be directly related to the major field of study listed on your DS-2019.
- **Approved before your program ends:** AT must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date.
- **Timely start:** AT must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.

**Time limits that also apply:**
- Bachelor's and master's students: up to 18 months (or the length of the degree program, if shorter). STEM degree students may qualify for a special extension.
- PhD students: up to 36 months (or the length of the degree program, if shorter).
- Non-degree students: the DS-2019 can't extend beyond 24 months total, including the degree program and AT.

**Proposed rule:** ISSS posted an announcement (September 16, 2025) about a DHS proposal to replace duration of status with fixed periods of stay. If it is implemented, J-1 students would need to apply to USCIS for an extension to do post-graduation AT. It is described as a proposal, and I didn't find anything in the excerpts saying it has taken effect.

To confirm whether you qualify, please check with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Tôi được phép thất nghiệp bao nhiêu ngày?
history: Tôi đang làm OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp.
records.search_query: Tôi được phép thất nghiệp bao nhiêu ngày? | Tôi đang làm OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp.
records.answer:
Bạn được phép thất nghiệp tối đa **90 ngày** trong thời gian OPT sau tốt nghiệp 12 tháng. Nếu sau đó bạn được duyệt gia hạn **STEM OPT 24 tháng**, bạn được thêm **60 ngày**, tức tối đa **150 ngày** thất nghiệp cộng dồn.

**Cách tính:**
- Mỗi ngày (kể cả cuối tuần) kể từ ngày bắt đầu OPT trên thẻ EAD mà bạn không có việc làm phù hợp đều được tính là một ngày thất nghiệp.
- Nếu mất việc hoặc có gián đoạn việc làm, bạn phải báo cho ISSS. Trong giai đoạn STEM OPT, bạn còn phải nộp bản đánh giá cuối cùng trên Form I-983 trong vòng 10 ngày nếu nghỉ hoặc mất việc.

**Nếu sắp chạm giới hạn:** Vượt quá giới hạn mà không có hành động phù hợp (như chuyển trường, đổi bậc học, rời Mỹ hoặc hành động khác để duy trì tình trạng) là vi phạm tình trạng F-1. Bạn phải thực hiện một trong các hành động đó **trước** ngày thất nghiệp cuối cùng.

**Lưu ý về thay đổi sắp tới:** Ngày 28/08/2026, ISSS đăng thông báo rằng DHS dự kiến đề xuất bỏ thời gian ân hạn 60 ngày đối với một số lao động không định cư sau khi chấm dứt việc làm. Tôi chỉ thấy tiêu đề thông báo, không có chi tiết, nên bạn hãy hỏi cố vấn ISSS xem điều này có ảnh hưởng đến bạn không.

Về tình huống cụ thể của bạn, hãy xác nhận với cố vấn ISSS.
